summary: Gustav Roth was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at several universities, earning his doctorate at Munich (1949–1952) and studying at Patna (1952–1956). He served at the University of Göttingen (1965–1981) and directed Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1982–1985).

Gustav Salomon Oppert worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig, Bonn, Halle-Wittenberg (~1859–1860), and the Berlin University of the Arts, where he later held a post from around 1894 to 1908.
Gustavo Benavides is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who held posts at Villanova University, attested in 1995 and 2004.
Guus Kroonen is a linguist who completed his doctoral studies under Alexander Lubotsky (~2005–2009). He later held academic posts at the University of Copenhagen (~2013) and Leiden University (2016).

Guy G. Stroumsa works in religious studies. After studying at Paris, Hebrew University, EPHE, and Harvard (PhD 1978), he held various posts at Hebrew University (1978–2009) and served as Emeritus Professor of the Study of Abrahamic Religions at Oxford (2009–2013).

Guy Newland is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981) and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Central Michigan University (attested 1996–2010).
Gyal Rong Tendzin Drakpa studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Gyatsho Tshering was a scholar of Tibetology who studied at the University of Calcutta. He founded the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, serving as its acting director in 1972 and director from 1974 to 1998.

Gyoei Fukuda was a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Tendai Daigakurin. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1928), Toyo University, and served as president of Taisho University (~1940–1943).

Gyoei Takahashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts at Rissho University (attested 2003–2004 and 2026) and served as a staff member at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 2004).

Gyoko Iotani is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1968–1978). He served at Rissho University as associate professor, professor, and emeritus professor (~1982–2017), and held a post at Minobusan University (~2017).
Gyokusen Hosaka was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. He served as president of Komazawa Junior College from approximately 1950 to 1963.
Gyomay Kubose was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at Otani University and under Haya Akegarasu from around 1928 to 1932.
Gyoon Iotani is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Waseda University (attested 2015) and held a post as deputy director at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
Gyosho Takahashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1992) and Minobusan University (attested 1996).
Gyoshu Chojo is a Buddhist studies scholar who held professorships at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1996) and the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Minobusan University (attested 2001).
Gyula Ortutay studied at the University of Szeged (1928–1934) and held a post at Nyugat.

Gyurme Dorje was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Edinburgh and SOAS, earning his PhD under Philip Denwood (~1982–1987), held fellowships at SOAS/University of London (1991–1996), and worked as a translator for Tsadra Foundation (2007–2020).
Gyurme Pema Tekchok studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
György Hazai was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1949–1954) and held a post at the Institut für Orientforschung (~1963–1982).
